passages.original: ἐξέσται δὲ αὐτὸν ἀπαγαγόντα βραχύ τι τῆς τραπέζης βλέπειν εἰς τὰ σκέλη τοῦ τείνοντος αὐτὸν ἡ εἰς τὰ προκείμενα. ἀκούομεν δὲ οἶόν τι καὶ Δημο- σθένης διηγεῖτο ἐν θιάσοις καὶ πεπωκόσιν ἀνθρώποις στρέφεσθαι νέον καὶ ὅτι μεγίστῳ τούτῳ κατὰ τῶν Αἰσχίνῃ βεβιωμένων κέχρηται μαρτυρίῳ.
passages.english: And it will be possible for him, drawing [his eyes] away a little from the table, to look at the legs of the one who is serving him or at the dishes set before [him]. And we hear what sort of thing Demosthenes too related: that a young man moved about in revel-companies and among people who had been drinking; and that he used this as the greatest piece of evidence against the life Aeschines had led.
passages.notes: Libanius, Oration 53 (against the invitation of boys to banquets). 'Demo- sthenes' is a line-break split for Demosthenes. The phrase τοῦ τείνοντος αὐτὸν is difficult. It is rendered here as 'the one serving him', but it may be corrupt, perhaps for something like 'the one handing [things] to him'. In the second sentence the syntax of στρέφεσθαι νέον is loose and the sense is uncertain. It appears to refer to Demosthenes' charge that Aeschines as a youth went about among thiasoi and drinkers. 'Ολύμπαι' in the context is probably a misreading for Ὀλύμπια.
